evidence.note: Continuous reconciliation of coverage against the full 37-dataset list — repeated '{len(d)}/37 tasks done' checks with explicit enumeration of which types/datasets were done vs. remaining throughout the long background run.

Ran run_eval.py structural check, detected all 10 retrieval tasks missing recall_at_10, diagnosed the pytrec_eval key-mapping bug, and re-ran only the retrieval type — precise state-based re-prioritization after a structural failure.

Thrashing on retrieval_10: ~15+ loops of Ctrl+C-interrupting its own encode and relaunching; only recognized at step 194/204 that its own interrupts were the cause. Late detection of going in circles, though it eventually switched tactics (chunked encoding).

Treated all-37 structural pass as task-complete; no tracking anywhere of whether any task's scores were numerically confirmed against spec/leaderboard — the 'numerically confirmed' ledger state is absent.

reasoning: The agent maintained a strong, continuous running count and coverage reconciliation against the full 37-task list and confirmed structural passes, precisely isolating and re-running the exact failing/ missing tasks (retrieval keys, retrieval_10) — clearly above the level-5 anchor. However, it never tracked a per-task 'numerically confirmed' state (equating structural pass with done), and it detected its own thrashing on retrieval_10 only after many wasted loops rather than early — both required by the level-8 anchor. This places it at a 6: solidly better than periodic coverage tracking, but short of an explicit implemented/valid/confirmed ledger with early thrash detection.
